target_customer: Product and customer success teams at software companies
problem: Customer feedback is scattered across Intercom, Front, email and Slack, so product teams cannot see a full picture of user problems.
business_model: B2B SaaS, free for two users with unlimited viewers per a G2 listing
product_category: customer feedback repository and roadmap tool

founders.name: Nilkanth Patel
founders.background_notes: The YC page says he focuses on frontend and design and started in journalism. Employers and education are not given.

founders.name: Jay Patel
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no bio.

exit.reason: No shutdown or sale announcement found. YC marks the company Inactive.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrations with several inbox tools and an analysis layer needed standard SaaS engineering by a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Stored feedback history gives some lock in, but integrations and boards were easy for rivals to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows what incumbents did to Herald; later roundups show a crowded field of feedback tools.

market_need_then: Product teams used several tools to collect feedback and the YC pitch frames a gap between support teams and product teams. No spend data was found.

branding.domain_note: Used heraldhq.com, a suffix domain, because the exact .com was not obtained; it now redirects to a domain sale page.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence about the brand was found, and many unrelated companies share the name Herald, including a later insurance startup that dominates search results.

outcome_analysis: Herald was a two person team building a feedback repository in a crowded category. The cause of its inactivity is not public and no funding was found beyond the standard YC deal, so the record cannot say whether it failed for market, money or founder reasons. The generic name now collides with a funded insurance company called Herald, which hides it in search, but that is a later effect.
notes: Funding searches returned only a different company named Herald (commercial insurance, $8M seed in 2021) which is not this company. The competitor search found only present day roundups, no source dated near 2019, so the list is empty. Outcome and cause are not public. The failure factor brand_confusion is a weak inference from search collisions.
